what: server-side timestamp for a pre-registration published before firing
why: A commit's author and committer dates are set locally and prove nothing to a reader. GitHub's PushEvent time is recorded server-side and is the artifact that actually evidences ordering. Public events expire from the API after roughly 90 days, so the receipt is archived here while it is still live.
limits: This file is our archive of GitHub's statement. While the event remains queryable a third party can confirm it independently; afterwards they are trusting this copy. A signed commit or an external timestamp anchor would be strictly stronger and is the obvious next hardening.
